REngine.jar contains the org.rosuda.REngine classes which are backend-independent.

RserveEngine.jar contains the Rserve back-end classes for the above REngine.

You need both to use a REngine-based Rserve client.

Just in case you wondered other back-end is for example JRI: http://rforge.net/JRI/files/
The benefit is that your code should work unchanged for all REngines regardless of the back-end.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
On Sep 12, 2010, at 8:34 AM, Suresh Krishna wrote:

> 
>> Maybe this is more of a R question than a Rserve question: but when does one use eval and when does one use parseAndEval from the java client ? Looking at test.java in the source, I am unable to figure this out..
> 
> To clarify further, I thought I understood that eval takes an REXP as input while parseAndEval takes a text string as input (that parse converts into an R expression). So I guess I am puzzled by the difference between an REXP input and a string input:
> 
> 
> 			REXP df = c.parseAndEval("{data(iris); iris}");
> 			c.assign("df", df);
> 			REXP x = c.eval("identical(df, iris)");
> 
> Why does the first statement use parseAndEval while the second one uses eval ?
> 

There is no eval(String) in the REngine API - there is only

REXP eval(REXP what, REXP where, boolean resolve) 
          evaluate an expression vector

which takes an expression REXP and environment. evalAndParse(String) parses the expression and evaluates it in the global environment.

There is eval(String) in the RConnection class for compatibility with the old JRclient, but it is NOT part of the REngine API (so if you used the API correctly [access REngine and not RConnection] the compiler would tell you).

Cheers,
Simon

e = .jcall("org/rosuda/REngine/REngine", "Lorg/rosuda/REngine/REngine;", "getLastEngine")
if (is.jnull(e)) e = .jnew("org/rosuda/REngine/JRI/JRIEngine", .jengine())

Simon

messages.subject: rJava: Problems with .jarray
messages.body_plain:
Dear Developers,

I started to work with your nice package 'rJava' (version 0.8-7) for getting 
some of my probabilistic models runing in R. Everything works fine so far.

I already emailed the following problem to Simon Urbanek. Simon kindly wrote 
me that I should mail to this list and maybe that Romain could help me with 
the following problem.

For passing input from R to Java, I have initially written the two following 
test functions:

public double[][] returnDMatrix( double[][] m )
{
        return m;               
}
        
public double[][][] returnDTensor( double[][][] m )
{
        return m;
}

that I call with

returnDMatrix <- function( L )
{
        L <- .jarray( as.array( as.numeric( L ) ) )
        hjw <- .jnew( "HelloJavaWorld" )          
        out <- .jrcall( hjw, "returnDMatrix", L )       
        return( out )
}

returnDTensor <- function( L )
{
        hjw <- .jnew( "HelloJavaWorld" )
        out <- .jrcall( hjw, "returnDTensor", L )       
        return( out )
}

The following call works fine:

>aaa <- .jarray(array( as.numeric( 1:4 ), dim = c( 2, 2 ) ) )
> returnDMatrix( aaa )
>    [,1] [,2]
>[1,]    1    3
>[2,]    2    4

However, when I call the function returnDTensor

> aaa <- .jarray(array( as.numeric( 1:8 ), dim = c( 2, 2, 2 ) ) )
> returnDTensor( aaa )

I get the following result

>, , 1
>
>     [,1] [,2]
>[1,]    1    0
>[2,]    0    4
>
>, , 2
>
>     [,1] [,2]
>[1,]    5    0
>[2,]    0    8

but I would expect

> array( as.numeric( 1:8 ), dim = c( 2, 2, 2 ) )
>, , 1
>
>     [,1] [,2]
>[1,]    1    3
>[2,]    2    4
>
>, , 2
>
 >    [,1] [,2]
>[1,]    5    7
>[2,]    6    8

Are I'm doing something wrong or is this a bug? How can I transfer 3d-Array 
correctly to Java?


Hope to hear from you.

Many thanks and Best Regards,

Michael
